'Give me a child until he is seven, and I will give you the man.' This Jesuit motto has opened every episode of director Michael Apted's ground-breaking Up series, which has endeavoured to catch up with the same 14 people every seven years since 1964, when they were seven years old. Now, in the final show - without Apted, who died in 2021 - those children are 70. So as they look back on their lives, does that adage still ring true? No one is untouched by change. Some have had happy lives, others not so much. Bruce Balden was at boarding school when he was chosen, and he became a teacher. 'I do see myself in that seven-year-old,' he says. 'I don't know whether some aspects of my character are immutable or I've changed. But I see a rather lost soul. I want to reassure him that it will be a ride, but life is going to be all right.' Seven-year-old Bruce just wanted to see his father, a soldier in Southern Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe). Now he reads a poem in which his dad explains his feelings for his son. 'He missed me as much as I missed him. If I'd known, I'd have made more of an effort to make up for lost time.'
